what: Affirm provides buy-now-pay-later financing. Shoppers split purchases into instalments at checkout, and Affirm earns from merchant fees and from interest on longer loans, which it funds and partly sells on.
customers: Online and in-store shoppers, and merchants including Amazon, Walmart and Shopify sellers who offer it at checkout.
money: fees paid by merchants for offering the option
selling loans to funding partners and servicing them
moat: Underwriting built on transaction-level data rather than credit scores, plus exclusive placements at the largest online checkouts in the United States.
risks: Credit losses rise when consumers come under pressure
Debt of about $10 billion funds the loan book
Regulators have signalled tighter rules for buy-now-pay-later lending
Losing a large merchant partner would remove a meaningful share of volume
opportunities: Revenue grew about 32% last year and about 39% a year over three years
Analysts see large upside, with a median target well above the current price
The Affirm Card extends it from checkout financing into everyday spending
watch: Gross merchandise volume growth and the delinquency rate on loans.
